Floor and ceiling functions

Words: 74 Articles: 3
Calculus OurBigBook.com
The floor and ceiling functions round a real number x to the nearest enclosing integers: ⌊x⌋ is the greatest integer at most x, and ⌈x⌉ is the least integer at least x. They satisfy ⌈x⌉=−⌊−x⌋.

Floor function (⌊x⌋)

Words: 23 Articles: 1
Floor and ceiling functions OurBigBook.com
The floor ⌊x⌋ is the greatest integer not exceeding the real number x.

Fractional part ({x})

Words: 9
Floor function OurBigBook.com
The fractional part of a real number is {x}=x−⌊x⌋∈[0,1).

Ceiling function (⌈x⌉)

Words: 12
Floor and ceiling functions OurBigBook.com
The ceiling function gives the least integer greater than or equal to its input real number.

Calculus OurBigBook.com
An integral accumulates a function over a domain and may be defined as a limit of finite sums.

Wallis integrals (In​=∫0π/2​sinnxdx)

Words: 51
Integral OurBigBook.com
The Wallis integrals are In​=∫0π/2​sinnxdx for integers n≥0. Integration by parts gives nIn​=(n−1)In−2​ for n≥2, with I0​=π/2, I1​=1. Hence
I2n​=22n(n!)2(2n)!​2π​,I2n+1​=(2n+1)!22n(n!)2​.
(1)
Because 0<sinx<1 in the integration interval, 0<In​<In−1​ for n≥1. Combining this with the recurrence gives 2n/(2n+1)<I2n+1​/I2n​<1, proving that the ratio tends to one and yielding the Wallis product.

Dipole line-integral identity (∫0c​∣r−tr0​∣3r−tr0​​dt=rPc​(rPc​+r⋅Pc​)c(Pc​r+rPc​)​)

Words: 66
Integral OurBigBook.com
Here r=∣r∣, Pc​=r−cr0​ and Pc​=∣Pc​∣. The identity holds where the segment of source points tr0​, 0≤t≤c, avoids the observation point and the denominator is nonzero. Differentiating the right side with respect to c gives the integrand and its value at c=0 is zero. Dotting with a current dipole moment evaluates a continuous line of dipole electric potentials.

Integrand (f(x))

Words: 30
Integral OurBigBook.com
In ∫ab​f(x)dx, the function f is the integrand. It is distinct from the integration variable, the bounds and the resulting integral. In contour integration, the transformed integrand includes the parametrization derivative.

Multiple integral (∫D​f(x1​,…,xn​)dx1​⋯dxn​)

Words: 89 Articles: 1
Integral OurBigBook.com
A multiple integral accumulates a function over a region with several coordinates. The Fubini theorem and Tonelli theorem give conditions under which it equals successive one-dimensional integrals. A change of variables formula expresses it in new coordinates using the absolute Jacobian determinant.

Odd-integrand cancellation by reflection

Words: 57
Multiple integral OurBigBook.com
If a region is invariant under one coordinate reflection and an integrable function changes sign under that reflection, its multiple integral is zero. Apply the change of variables formula to the reflection, whose absolute Jacobian determinant is one: the integral equals its negative. This applies to odd coordinate powers in symmetric volumes and to the off-diagonal entries of an inertia tensor when the mass density shares the coordinate-reflection symmetries.

Integral representation

Words: 121 Articles: 3
Integral OurBigBook.com
An integral representation expresses a function through an integral of specified data and an integral kernel. Green-function representations solve differential equations this way, while the Bromwich inversion formula reconstructs a function from its Laplace transform.

Trigonometric integral (Si(x), Ci(x))

Words: 97 Articles: 2
Integral representation OurBigBook.com
The sine and cosine integrals accumulate sint/t and cost/t, with different normalizations at zero and infinity. They arise in oscillatory integrals, Fourier transforms of singular kernels and Fourier series of logarithmic profiles.
Cosine integral (Ci(x)=−∫x∞​cost/tdt)
Words: 33
Trigonometric integral OurBigBook.com
For real x>0, its small-argument expansion is Ci(x)=γE​+logx+O(x2). Integrating Ci′(x)=cosx/x separates the logarithm from the regular correction. Its conventional constant is the Euler--Mascheroni constant; the primary series normalization is dlmf.nist.gov/6.6.E6 .
Sine integral (Si(x)=∫0x​sint/tdt)
Words: 34
Trigonometric integral OurBigBook.com
For real x>0, the sine integral approaches π/2. Exponential damping gives ∫0∞​e−atsint/tdt=arctan(1/a), so the limiting constant follows by letting a↓0. Integration by parts of the tail gives Si(x)=π/2−cosx/x−sinx/x2+O(x−3).

Lebesgue integration

Words: 103 Articles: 2
Integral OurBigBook.com
Lebesgue integration constructs an integral from the measure of level sets or from approximation by simple functions. It is linear on integrable functions and is stable under the principal convergence theorems of measure theory.

Prékopa–Leindler inequality (∫h≥(∫f)1−θ(∫g)θ)

Words: 34
Lebesgue integration OurBigBook.com
If 0<θ<1 and nonnegative measurable functions satisfy h((1−θ)x+θy)≥f(x)1−θg(y)θ for all x,y∈Rn, then their Lebesgue integrals obey
∫h≥(∫f)1−θ(∫g)θ.
(2)
The quantile derivative identity and monotone substitution inequality prove the one-dimensional case; Tonelli theorem extends it by induction. It implies the Brunn–Minkowski inequality.

Absolute continuity of the Lebesgue integral

Words: 36
Lebesgue integration OurBigBook.com
If f∈L1, then for every ε>0 there is δ>0 such that ∫E​∣f∣<ε whenever the measure of E is below δ. In particular, integrals over a sequence of shrinking measurable sets tend to zero.

Time integral (∫dt)

Words: 26
Integral OurBigBook.com
A time integral accumulates an integrand over a time coordinate. In perturbation theory it commonly sums the effect of an interaction over all possible vertex times.

Double integral (∬)

Integral OurBigBook.com
A double integral integrates a function over a two-dimensional region. A change of variables formula can replace the region and area element using a Jacobian determinant.
It is a multiple integral with two integration variables.

If measurable functions satisfy f≤g almost everywhere, then
∫fdμ≤∫gdμ

whenever the two sides are defined.

Antiderivative

Words: 98 Articles: 2
Integral OurBigBook.com
An antiderivative of g is a differentiable function p satisfying p′=g.

Constant of integration (∫f(x)dx=F(x)+C)

Words: 61
Antiderivative OurBigBook.com
If F′=f on a connected interval, every other antiderivative is F+C for a constant C. Indeed (G−F)′=0, so the mean value theorem makes G−F constant. A boundary condition fixes C. For example T′=−B/r2 integrates to T=B/r+C, and T(Rs​)=Ts​ gives C=Ts​−B/Rs​. Discarding an integration constant therefore needs an actual boundary condition or an approximation showing that its effect is small.

Additive constant

Words: 27
Antiderivative OurBigBook.com
Any two antiderivatives of the same function on a connected interval differ by an additive constant.
When parameterizing all antiderivatives, the arbitrary additive constant is the constant of integration.

Gaussian integral (∫−∞∞​e−x2dx=π​)

Words: 353 Articles: 8
Integral OurBigBook.com
The Gaussian integral is
∫−∞∞​e−ax2dx=aπ​​,a>0.
(4)
Squaring the integral and changing to polar coordinates proves the formula.

Linear-source multivariate Gaussian integral (∫Rn​e−uTAu/2+bTudu=(2π)n/2(detA)−1/2ebTA−1b/2)

Words: 56
Gaussian integral OurBigBook.com
For real symmetric positive-definite A, complete the square with v=u−A−1b. Orthogonal diagonalization reduces the remaining integral to the product of one-dimensional Gaussian integrals, proving the displayed expression. Positivity ensures convergence and the positive determinant square root. Replacing matrices by regulated field kernels gives the Gaussian functional integral; an oscillatory Minkowski integral instead requires a causal convergence prescription.

Dawson function (FD​(z)=e−z2∫0z​eu2du)

Words: 72 Articles: 1
Gaussian integral OurBigBook.com
The Dawson function obeys FD′​+2zFD​=1 by differentiation. Its large-real-argument asymptotic expansion begins FD​(z)=1/(2z)+1/(4z3)+O(z−5). This inverse-power behavior contrasts with the separate exponentially growing factors in its definition.
Gaussian drift primitives (E0​(z), E1​(z))
Words: 47
Dawson function OurBigBook.com
Define E0​(z)=∫0z​e−t2∫0t​eu2dudt and E1​(z)=∫0z​e−t2∫0t​eu2erfududt. They satisfy (D2+2zD)E0​=1 and (D2+2zD)E1​=erfz. The first is an even function, the second an odd function, and their real tails are respectively 21​log∣z∣+C1​+o(1) and sgnz[21​log∣z∣+C2​+o(1)]. Their derivatives have inverse-linear tails, explaining the logarithmic matching constants in a singular perturbation.

Error function (erf)

Words: 206 Articles: 4
Gaussian integral OurBigBook.com
The error function is
erf(x)=π​2​∫0x​e−u2du.
(5)
It is odd and tends to ±1 as x→±∞.
Quadrant asymptotics of the error function (∫0z​e−t2dt)
Words: 68
Error function OurBigBook.com
For z=reiθ with fixed 0≤θ≤π/2, a horizontal tail gives f(z)=π​/2−e−z2(2z)−1[1+O(z−2)]. The constant dominates through θ=π/4; above that angle the exponential endpoint dominates. At the boundary angle its modulus is only O(r−1), so the constant remains leading. On the imaginary axis the integral is purely imaginary and grows as ier2/(2r). The approximation is not a determination of exponentially subdominant constants in that growing sector.
Complementary error function (erfcz=1−erfz)
Words: 123 Articles: 2
Error function OurBigBook.com
The complementary error function avoids subtracting a quantity close to one when describing a small Gaussian integral tail. For real x>0, erfcx=(2/π​)∫x∞​e−t2dt; analytic continuation defines it for complex arguments.
Faddeeva function (w(z)=e−z2erfc(−iz))
Words: 97 Articles: 1
Complementary error function OurBigBook.com
The Faddeeva function is an entire function built from the complementary error function. Its integral representation for Imz>0 is w(z)=(iπ)−1∫−∞∞​e−t2/(t−z)dt, as normalized in NIST's integral representation. Its reflection identity is w(−z)=2e−z2−w(z), directly from the odd function property of the error function.
Gaussian pole integral (G(a)=∫−∞∞​e−s2/4/(s−a)ds)
Words: 60
Faddeeva function OurBigBook.com
For a pole off the real axis, substitution s=2t into the Faddeeva function integral gives G(a)=iπw(a/2) when Ima>0, and G(a)=−iπw(−a/2) when Ima<0. The difference of boundary values is the residue theorem jump 2πie−a2/4. In particular, for a lower-half-plane pole, G(a)+2πie−a2/4=iπw(a/2), which packages a crossed residue and a nearby saddle into one smooth expression.

e (mathematical constant, e)

Words: 85 Articles: 1
Exponential function OurBigBook.com
Euler's number is the value exp(1)=∑n=0∞​1/n! of the exponential function, approximately 2.71828. It is the base of the natural logarithm. Its factorial-series tail gives an elementary proof of the irrationality of e.

Irrationality of e (e∈/Q)

Words: 55
e (mathematical constant) OurBigBook.com
If Euler's number were a/b, choose n≥max(b,2) and multiply its factorial-series tail by n!. This produces an integer, but the tail is positive and smaller than ∑j≥1​(n+1)−j=1/n<1. The contradiction proves that the number is an irrational number. The argument illustrates how a rapidly convergent rational series can force a hypothetical rational remainder into an impossible integer interval.

ex=∑n=0∞​n!xn​.

For a Hadamard differentiable functional with continuous linear derivative L, define Rt​(h)=(Φ(s+th)−Φ(s))/t−L(h). For every compact K and positive ϵ, some positive δ,a make ∣Rt​(h)∣<ϵ whenever dist(h,K)<δ and 0<∣t∣<a. If this failed, choose tj​→0, directions within 1/j of K and remainders at least ϵ. Compactness gives a convergent subsequence of nearby points of K, hence convergent directions. The derivative definition and continuity of L give remainder tending to zero, a contradiction. With a tight weak limit, the Portmanteau theorem makes random directions lie near a suitable compact set with arbitrarily large probability. Thus this lemma proves the functional delta method without assuming separability of the entire normed space or uniform differentiability on its whole unit ball.

A differentiable map on a connected open subset of Euclidean space whose derivative vanishes everywhere is constant. The mean value inequality makes it constant on every ball in the domain, hence locally constant; connectedness then makes the value global.

The displayed smooth map from R2 to the punctured plane has Jacobian determinant one: in polar coordinates its radius is es and its angle is re−2s, so the determinant is e2se−2s=1. Nevertheless a(0,2πk)=(1,0) for every integer k. Thus a local volume-preserving map need not be injective or have bounded weighted inverse multiplicity. Compactly supported data distributed over many inverse branches disprove a determinant-only dispersion with a nonlinear velocity map estimate.

Odd extension

Words: 55
Odd function OurBigBook.com
An odd extension of a function f on the positive half-line is f​(r)=f(r) for r>0 and f​(r)=−f(−r) for r<0. At zero it is set to zero when the boundary value is zero. Smoothness requires compatible even derivatives at zero. In the radial reduction of the three-dimensional wave equation, rϕ(t,r) has a smooth odd extension whenever ϕ is smooth and radial.
